title: Maximum Profit From Trading Stocks
summary: Choose any subset of distinct stocks to buy now within the budget and sell later; return the maximum total profit.
statement: Choose any subset of distinct stocks to buy now within the budget and sell later; return the maximum total profit.
constraints: Each stock may be bought at most once at its present price, and any number of distinct stocks may be selected.
Total purchase cost cannot exceed budget; unspent money is allowed.
Profit for a selected stock is future[i]-present[i], and loss-making stocks may be skipped.
hints: This is 0/1 knapsack with present price as weight and positive future-minus-present as value.
Process each stock once and update budgets in descending order to prevent reusing it.
For money from budget down to cost, maximize dp[money] with dp[money-cost]+profit.
Descending updates preserve the previous-stock layer, so every feasible subset is represented once and the maximum profit is retained.
editorial: Descending updates preserve the previous-stock layer, so every feasible subset is represented once and the maximum profit is retained.

tests.explanation: Buying stocks costing five, two, and three uses the budget and earns 3+1+2=6.
Only the cost-two stock is affordable and profitable, earning three.
